app.title: BioManager: lab colony and stock manager
app.summary: A person opens a home page that lists what needs doing today: weanings due, the genotyping queue, animals not weighed and other reminders. They keep the colony in sheets they edit like a spreadsheet: one row per animal and one per cage, filtered by owner, cage purpose or search, with batch actions on the selected rows. They place cages on a drag-and-drop rack grid. On a breeding cage they record a birth, then genotyping, which creates the litter and its pups, then weaning, which sends the pups to new or existing cages. They can export the animal list, and every batch change goes into a history that can be undone.

task.text: Keep a breeding animal colony's animals, cages, litters and rack positions up to date over time, and show what husbandry work is due.

data.text: Linked records of individual animals, their housing units, litters, strains and racks, with dates that set when the next husbandry steps are due.
data.item: an animal, or a cage of animals at a position in a rack

stage.text: keeping the animal colony in order day to day, alongside breeding and experiments

mechanism.text: Editable sheets of animals, cages and litters are the main record. The home dashboard and the calendar are worked out from their dates (birth, weaning at P21, genotyping at P28). A rack grid shows the same cages by position and moves them by drag, and per-cage actions (Litter born, Genotyping, Wean) step a breeding cage through its litter's stages.

field.text: animal colony and breeding management in a biology lab

workflow.name: keep a living collection's records and schedule up to date

steps.step: see what work is due today
steps.here: Home lists upcoming weanings, the genotyping queue, animals that may need a look and reminders, all worked out from dates in the records
Add animals one by one or as a batch from a pasted grid with a preview, or import a CSV

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: My colony / Shared / Everyone scopes, the All · Active · per-purpose chips above the cages, and search

steps.step: edit records in place, one row or many at once
steps.here: Cells are edited like a spreadsheet; the selection bar applies a field, sacrifice, adding to an experiment or retiring cages to every selected row

steps.step: place items on a fixed layout
steps.here: Drag cage tiles onto rack positions or back to Unplaced (or Move, then tap). A position holding two living cages is marked !

steps.step: move an item through its stages
steps.here: On a Breeding cage: Litter born sets the weaning and genotyping dates; Genotyping takes the parents and pup count and makes the litter and its pups; Wean sends each pup row to a new or existing cage
Export the mouse sheet. Batch history lists each change and can undo it

distinctive: Each animal's age and life stage is shown by a coloured dot before its ID: under 8 weeks, 8 to 30 weeks, past 30 weeks, or not alive
Weaning and genotyping dates follow from the birth date (P21, P28, set by the lab), and weaning before P18 asks for confirmation first
Cage purposes are the lab's own list. Only a Breeding cage takes Litter born, Genotyping and Wean
Who owns a record and who it is shared with set who may edit it, separately from what each person can see
Weaning distributes the pups, females and males apart, into new or existing cages
